questions.question: Which sentence uses the present perfect correctly to describe an experience?
options: I have lived in London for five years.
I lived in London for five years.
I have lived in London since 2019.
I lived in London since 2019.
questions.answer: I have lived in London for five years.

questions.question: Choose the correct comparative form of the adjective 'busy'.
options: busier
more busy
busiest
busier than

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses a first conditional to express a future possibility?
options: If it rains, we will stay at home.
If it rained, we would stay at home.
If it rains, we will have stayed at home.
If it has rained, we will stay at home.
questions.answer: If it rains, we will stay at home.

questions.question: Select the sentence that correctly uses a gerund as the subject.
options: Swimming is good exercise.
To swim is good exercise.
Swim is good exercise.
Swimmingly is good exercise.

questions.question: Which sentence uses the modal 'should' to give advice?
options: You should eat more vegetables.
You must eat more vegetables.
You ought to eat more vegetables.
You can eat more vegetables.

questions.question: Complete the sentence with the correct past continuous form.
options: I was cooking dinner when the phone rang.
I cooked dinner when the phone rang.
I had cooked dinner when the phone rang.
I was cooking dinner while the phone rang.
questions.answer: I was cooking dinner when the phone rang.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses 'although' to show contrast?
options: Although it was raining, we went for a walk.
Although we went for a walk, it was raining.
We went for a walk although it was raining.
It was raining although we went for a walk.
questions.answer: Although it was raining, we went for a walk.

questions.question: Choose the sentence that correctly uses the superlative form.
options: This is the most delicious cake I have ever tasted.
This is more delicious cake than I have ever tasted.
This is delicious cake than I have ever tasted.
This is the most delicious cake I ever tasted.
questions.answer: This is the most delicious cake I have ever tasted.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses the infinitive after 'want'?
options: I want to go to the cinema.
I want going to the cinema.
I want go to the cinema.
I wanted to go to the cinema.
questions.answer: I want to go to the cinema.

questions.question: Select the sentence that uses the correct past simple tense.
options: She visited her grandmother yesterday.
She has visited her grandmother yesterday.
She was visiting her grandmother yesterday.
She had visited her grandmother yesterday.
